WD is building the infrastructure behind the AI-driven data economy.

As AI scales, so does data. Every interaction, every model, every system generates data that must be stored, managed, and made accessible over time. That’s where we come in.

We combine deep engineering expertise with global-scale manufacturing to deliver the storage systems that make AI possible, powering hyperscale data centers, cloud platforms, and enterprise infrastructure worldwide.

Who We Are

Vermeer equips customers doing important work around the world. We are global, driven by innovation and growing. The equipment we make manages natural resources, connects people and feeds and fuels communities. We live out a caring culture, we demonstrate agility, we keep a focus on customers and are stewards of our resources. These beliefs drive our culture, determine how we treat others and steer our business.

Work Shift

1 - First Shift

Job Summary

Are you passionate about embedded systems and excited to bring intelligent machines to life? As an Embedded Software Engineer Intern at Vermeer, you’ll help develop and test the software that powers our next-generation equipment. This internship offers hands-on experience, mentorship, and the opportunity to grow into a full-time engineering role upon graduation.

What You’ll Do

1. Assist in developing and testing embedded software using C, C++, or MATLAB/Simulink for real-time control systems.

2. Support integration and debugging of control systems using Controller Area Network (CAN) protocols (e.g., SAE J1939) and tools such as CANalyzer or Vector CANoe.

3. Help develop Human-Machine Interfaces (HMI) and contribute to User Interface/User Experience (UI/UX) design using platforms like Qt or LabVIEW.

4. Participate in Agile development practices and DevOps workflows, including Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) using tools such as Git and GitHub.

5. Collaborate with engineers to support system validation and documentation using Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) systems (e.g., Dassault Systems 3DX), including exposure to Engineering Change Notification (ECN) processes.

6. Learn about and support the application of functional safety standards such as ISO 26262 (International Organization for Standardization – Road Vehicles Functional Safety) and IEC 61508 (International Electrotechnical Commission – Functional Safety of Electrical/Electronic/Programmable Systems).

What We’re Looking For

- Currently pursuing a Bachelor's degree in Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field.

- Exposure to embedded programming and control systems through coursework or hands-on projects.

- Familiarity with CAN protocols, HMI development, and Real-Time Operating Systems (RTOS) such as FreeRTOS or VxWorks is a plus.

- Interest in robotics, automation, and software development for intelligent equipment.

- Strong communication, problem-solving, and collaboration skills with a growth mindset.

Travel

- Occasional travel is expected of this position.

Work Location

ONSITE: A team member’s day-to-day work is best done on a Vermeer campus. If work content can be occasionally completed at an offsite location, discuss potential arrangements with your manager.

Equal Opportunity Employer

At Vermeer Corporation, we believe in the value of your unique identity, background, and experiences. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, marital status, genetic information, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, veteran status or any other status protected by the law. Applicants requiring a reasonable accommodation due to a disability at any stage of the employment application process should contact Team Member Solutions at (641) 621-8767 or at hr@vermeer.com.

Interested? We’d love to get to know you.

The Opportunity:

The Summer Games is an innovative internship program that attracts some of the nation’s best and brightest students. The goal is to develop a breakthrough idea or solution for one of our customer's most pressing, complex, and multidimensional problems while developing valuable technical skills. This competitive and collaborative program attracts thousands of applicants each year. Simulating a real-world startup accelerator environment, the interns are divided into teams, each working on a different challenge project. Throughout the Games, interns receive mentorship from senior leaders, solve problems using Booz Allen’s products and unique engagement models, and leverage the power of collaboration in a team environment.

The summer culminates with a final Challenge Cup competition and presentation to senior leadership. A past winner took the challenge of helping blind individuals navigate by using new technology and developing a business and market penetration plan. Teams have also helped to develop an app that gives military commanders an easy way to track real-time and open-source information about developing situations, including sudden attacks, fighting human trafficking, and even tracking the spread of a disease worldwide.

Join us. The world can't wait.

About the company

General Matter enriches uranium.

We are designing, building, and operating the world’s lowest-cost enrichment services, here in the US.

In the process, we are restoring America’s ability to produce nuclear fuel to power AI, advanced manufacturing and critical industries our country relies on to remain competitive.

Fuel drives the cost of advanced reactor electricity production, and enrichment drives the cost of the fuel that advanced reactors consume. Reliable, low-cost enrichment is the catalyst for the nuclear Renaissance now under way.

Our mission is to make nuclear not only the cleanest and safest source of baseload power, but also the most affordable. We believe abundant nuclear energy will lead to a post-scarcity society.

We were incubated inside Founders Fund, like Anduril and Palantir before us, and are backed by over a dozen of the world's top venture capital firms.

Our lean, world-class team of engineers and operators is applying a first-principles approach to solving the problem of nuclear fuel production.

We are a mission-driven company with a culture of urgency, accountability, and transparency.

Help us build a high-energy society by making the cleanest, safest form of baseload energy the most affordable.

About This Role

As a General Matter Software Engineering Intern, you will help develop performant, safe, and high-quality software. Your work will support code where reliability, performance, and safety are of utmost importance. You will work closely with cross-functional teams, including electrical engineers, software engineers, chemical engineers, manufacturing engineers, nuclear engineers, materials scientists, and physicists. If you seek high-impact work and are excited by fast-paced, intense, Skunkworks-style projects, we encourage you to reach out to join our team.

We're hiring interns across three focus areas:

- Backend interns will help build high-performance services and APIs that coordinate control systems, manage state across distributed hardware, and expose interfaces for monitoring and operations.

- Distributed systems interns will support the development of fault-tolerant coordination systems, real-time data pipelines processing high-throughput sensor telemetry, and the infrastructure that keeps critical systems running reliably at scale.

- Tooling interns will help build the developer platforms, CI/CD systems, observability tools, and deployment infrastructure that let our team iterate rapidly and safely in a production environment where mistakes have physical consequences.

Responsibilities

- Assist in designing and implementing high-performance software systems in C++ and Python, with a focus on reliability and maintainability.

- Support the architecture of solutions, contributing to decisions around system design, performance trade-offs, and technology selection.

- Participate in technical design reviews and code reviews, learning and helping uphold engineering best practices across the team.

- Help build and maintain automated testing and CI/CD pipelines to support software quality at scale.

- Work closely with senior engineers, contributing to progress on complex, ambiguous technical problems.

Basic Qualifications

- Current undergraduate or graduate student pursuing a degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related discipline.

- Proficiency in C++ and/or Python.

- Strong CS fundamentals, such as algorithms, data structures, concurrency, and system design.

- Collaborative team member who thrives in fast-paced, multidisciplinary environments and is eager to learn.

Preferred Skills and Experience

- Exposure to distributed systems, observability tooling, or infrastructure as code.

- Experience with Python ecosystems for data pipelines, automation, or backend services.

- Coursework or project experience with C++ performance optimization, profiling, or low-level systems programming.

- Familiarity with Linux system programming, including threading models, IPC, or low-level kernel interfaces.

- Evidence of exceptional ability (prior projects, portfolio of work, completed products, etc).

Additional Requirements

- Ability to work extended hours and weekends as necessary.

Equal Opportunity Employer

General Matter is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with General Matter is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.

Compensation and Benefits

The hourly pay range for this internship is $32–$46 per hour, depending on the candidate's current standing in school (i.e. sophomore, senior).

Interns will receive a monthly housing stipend and are eligible for overtime pay. Please note that the stated hourly range is an estimate and may be adjusted based on market conditions, business needs, or other factors.

Data Engineering - Intern

About the Role: -

We are seeking a highly motivated and enthusiastic Data Engineering Intern at the graduate level to join our dynamic team. The successful candidate will have the opportunity to gain practical experience with advanced data engineering technologies, including Databricks, SQL, Snowflake (data warehousing, Snowpark exposure is a plus), Python, PySpark, and Microsoft Azure. In addition, interns in this role will gain exposure to AI technologies and their implementation within data engineering workflows. This internship is well-suited for individuals who are eager to expand their technical skill set, collaborate with experienced professionals, and actively contribute to the design and implementation of large-scale data solutions.

- To apply, please submit your resume and a brief cover note outlining your interest and samples of your work.

- Location Chicago Hexaware Office, willingness to relocate for long term projects in the future is preferred

- We do not offer Visa Sponsorship or EAD processing for this internship

- Because we expect to consider these interns for full time employment upon completion of three months, we are only considering Previously Graduated or Spring 2026 Graduates. Based on organization requirements, interns may be considered for full time positions with full benefits. Others should reach out to us three months before their graduation date for the next session.

Expectations At the Internship Level: -

- Organizational Acumen: Develop a comprehensive understanding of the organization’s mission, values, and strategic objectives. Consistently align your contributions with the broader goals of the team and company.

- Commitment to Learning: Exhibit a proactive and enthusiastic approach to learning throughout the internship. Actively participate in training sessions, seek out opportunities for professional development, and demonstrate continual growth in both technical and business knowledge.

- Technical Proficiency: Acquire familiarity with the key technologies and tools utilized by the data engineering team, including but not limited to Databricks, SQL, PySpark, Snowflake (data warehousing, Snowpark exposure is a plus) and Azure DevOps. Strive to deepen your practical skills in these areas through hands-on project work.

- Increasing Autonomy: Begin your internship by working under general supervision, with the expectation of progressively taking on greater responsibility and executing tasks with increased independence as your experience and confidence grow.

- Collaborative Engagement: Operate effectively within a distributed and diverse global team environment. Demonstrate strong communication skills and a collaborative mindset while working with colleagues across various time zones and locations.

- AI Integration Exposure: Gain practical exposure to the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies within data engineering projects, enhancing your understanding of how advanced analytics and machine learning can drive business value.

Qualifications: -

Must Have Skills/Project Experience/Certifications: -

- Strong knowledge of Python, SQL, and PySpark (Scala optional)

- Experience building metadata-driven ingestion and data quality (DQ) frameworks using PySpark

- Solid grasp of Lakehouse architecture, Apache Spark, Delta Lake, and other key big data technologies

- Performance tuning in Databricks/Apache Spark

- Hands-on experience with artificial intelligence (AI) or machine learning (ML) projects is highly desirable. Exposure to integrating AI/ML models within data pipelines or familiarity with AI frameworks will be considered a significant advantage and may provide the candidate with a competitive edge in this role.

- Proven team collaboration abilities and excellent problem-solving and analytical skills

Education: -

- M.Sc (CS) degree or equivalent from accredited university or BS with strong Work or Internship Experience

- Relevant certifications in cloud, data engineering, or AI/ML are a plus.
